mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series 220d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series 220d engine replacement typically costs between £1,700 and £3,500 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt) and the specific engine code. Used engines start from around £1,100, reconditioned units from £1,700, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £2,400. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop. Main dealer replacement costs can exceed £4,200.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 2 Series 220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, which typically lasts 2-5 seconds before disappearing as oil pressure builds. This affects both N47-powered (2014-2015) and B47-powered (2015+) 220d models. Other symptoms include a metallic ticking sound, engine hesitation, and in severe cases, the engine management light illuminating with fault codes P000A, P0016, or P0017.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series 220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For an N47-powered 220d (2014-2015) worth £5,000-£8,000, a reconditioned engine at £1,700-£2,400 is often worthwhile if you plan to keep the car. For B47 models (2015+) worth £8,000-£15,000, replacement is almost always justified. For G42 models (2021+) worth £15,000+, replacement is a no-brainer. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series 220d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series 220d engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration. N47 timing chain replacement alone requires 12-18 hours of labour due to the rear-mounted chain.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N47 and B47 engine in the 220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 220d used the N47 engine from 2014-2015 (184hp, 380Nm torque) and the B47 from 2015 onwards (190hp, 400Nm torque). The B47 was introduced to address the N47's timing chain issues and improve emissions compliance. The B47 is generally more reliable, though it has its own EGR cooler and timing chain tensioner problems. Both are 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo diesels.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series 220d engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. For diesel 220d models, this includes DPF and EGR system validation to ensure compliance with UK emissions regulations.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series 220d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 2 Series 220d arrived in 2014 as the mid-range diesel variant across the 2 Series range, powered initially by the N47 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel engine producing 184hp. In 2015, the N47 was replaced by the revised B47 engine, bringing increased power to 188-190hp, improved reliability, and better emissions compliance.

milestones.description: N47D20O1, 2.0L turbo diesel, 184hp, 380Nm torque (F22 Coupe, F23 Convertible launch)
B47D20O0, 2.0L turbo diesel, 190hp, 400Nm torque (F22/F23, N47 replaced)
B47C20A, 2.0L transverse turbo diesel, 190hp (F45 Active Tourer, F46 Gran Tourer transverse mounting)
B47C20B, 2.0L transverse turbo diesel, 190hp (F45/F46 LCI update, emissions refinement)
B47D20O0, 2.0L turbo diesel, 190hp (G42 220d Coupe, new generation with mild updates)

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series 220d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3 (intro, 2-3 sentences): The BMW 2 Series 220d has been powered by two generations of 2.0-litre diesel engines: the earlier N47 (2014-2015) and the later B47 (2015-present). The N47 is notorious for timing chain failure, while the B47 suffers primarily from timing chain tensioner wear and EGR cooler cracking. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 2 Series 220d N47 Engine Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The N47 timing chain is located at the rear of the engine, making it inaccessible without removing the engine and gearbox. The chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch or snap. When the chain breaks, pistons strike valves, causing bent valves, damaged rocker arms, and often a written-off engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove engine, replace chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets, seals
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early (rattling noise only)

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if engine has suffered internal damage

problems.recommendation: If you own an N47-powered 220d and hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the timing chain inspected immediately - preventative replacement is significantly cheaper than a full rebuild after failure. If the chain has already snapped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N47D20O1 BMW 2 Series 220d engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - BMW 2 Series 220d B47 Diesel Rattle
problems.rootCause: The B47 uses a single-row timing chain system that has proven prone to premature stretch and guide wear. Unlike older multi-row chains, this design relies on a plastic tensioner rail that degrades faster under heat stress - especially in stop-start urban driving. BMW acknowledged the defect and issued Service Bulletin SI B11 02 17 confirming timing chain tensioner wear as a known weakness in pre-2018 models.

repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattle is persistent or mileage >70k

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £2,600-£3,500 (matches Section 4's rebuilt figure for B47 codes)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if chain has skipped teeth or caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - for a typical £8,000-£15,000 B47 220d, timing chain replacement is a worthwhile repair. Full engine replacement is justified if internal damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: The B47 timing chain issue is well-documented in BMW Service Bulletin SI B11 02 17. If you hear a metallic rattle on cold start lasting 2-5 seconds, have the car inspected immediately. A full timing chain kit replacement with upgraded components is the most cost-effective long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for B47 BMW 2 Series 220d engine replacement

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Cracking - BMW 2 Series 220d B47 Diesel Coolant Loss
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler on B47 engines can develop cracks, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating. The Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) issued Recall R/2019/241 covering EGR cooler leaks in B47D20A engines (2015-2018). In some cases, coolant mixing with exhaust gases can cause DPF blockages and further emissions system damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked EGR cooler with upgraded unit
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before DPF damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cooler, clean or replace DPF
repairOptions.longevity: Required if DPF is blocked by coolant contamination

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused head gasket or piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - for a typical £8,000-£15,000 B47 220d, EGR cooler replacement is a worthwhile repair. Only consider full engine replacement if overheating has caused secondary internal damage.
problems.recommendation: EGR cooler failure on the B47 is a critical issue covered by a DVSA recall. Check if your vehicle is affected at the GOV.UK Vehicle Recall Checker. Replace the cooler promptly if you notice coolant loss or a sweet smell from the exhaust. Upgraded metal-core EGR coolers are available and should be specified in any replacement to prevent recurrence.
